scenarios.name: Fed Policy Pivot to Rate Cuts
scenarios.description: Inflation continues to moderate toward the Fed's 2% target, prompting the FOMC to begin a gradual cutting cycle starting in Q1 2027. The federal funds rate declines by 75-100bps over 6-12 months as the Fed shifts from restrictive to neutral stance.

impacts.explanation: Fed cuts rates 75-100bps from current 3.88% as inflation normalizes
Long-term yields decline anticipating easier policy and lower term premium
Lower borrowing costs stimulate investment and consumption
Easier financial conditions support hiring and reduce layoffs
Rate cuts calibrated to avoid reigniting inflation; CPI remains near target
Lower mortgage rates revive homebuilder activity and buyer demand
Cheaper capital boosts manufacturing capex and durable goods
Lower rates improve consumer confidence and big-ticket spending
Job growth accelerates as businesses expand with cheaper financing
Lower interest expense reduces deficit growth modestly
Dollar impact offset by domestic demand; net neutral on trade

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Fed cutting cycles occur ~30% of years when rates are above neutral. Current restrictive stance (real rate ~1% with inflation at 3.8%) and lagged policy effects support pivot. Outside view: 1995, 2019 soft landing precedents. Inside view: Powell's data-dependence, shelter inflation lag, labor market cooling. Adjusted down from 35% to 30% due to fiscal dominance risks.

scenarios.name: Geopolitical Oil Shock from Middle East Escalation
scenarios.description: Regional conflict expands to disrupt Persian Gulf shipping lanes, removing 2-3M bpd of oil supply. Brent crude spikes to $110-130/bbl for 3-6 months, triggering global stagflationary pressures and risk-off capital flows.

impacts.explanation: Energy prices feed directly into CPI and indirectly via transport/input costs
Higher energy costs reduce real incomes and corporate margins
Fed hikes 50-75bps to anchor inflation expectations despite growth hit
Inflation premium rises; safe-haven demand partially offsets
Stagflation forces layoffs in energy-intensive sectors
Manufacturing hit by energy costs and supply chain disruptions
Gasoline price spike crowds out discretionary spending
Higher rates and consumer uncertainty depress housing
Job losses in transport, manufacturing, retail
Oil import bill surges; dollar strength hurts exports
Automatic stabilizers + potential fiscal stimulus increase borrowing

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Major Middle East oil disruptions ~15% per year (1973, 1979, 1990, 2019). Current tensions (Iran-Israel, Houthis, Gaza) elevate near-term risk. Tetlock adjustment: 18% reflects high tension but US strategic reserve, OPEC+ spare capacity, and demand destruction at high prices as mitigants. Commandment 5: clashing forces - escalation risk vs. diplomatic off-ramps.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem
Strive to distinguish as many degrees of doubt as the problem permits

scenarios.name: US-China Tech Decoupling Acceleration
scenarios.description: Bipartisan consensus hardens: comprehensive export controls on AI chips, quantum, biotech; investment screening; entity list expansion. China retaliates with critical mineral restrictions. Global supply chains fracture into parallel systems, raising costs and reducing efficiency.

impacts.explanation: Reshoring costs, component shortages, lost scale efficiencies
Productivity drag from supply chain duplication and trade diversion
Higher input costs from tariffs, compliance, less efficient sourcing
Export controls reduce US sales to China; import substitution costly
Fed tolerates higher rates to combat supply-side inflation
Term premium rises on geopolitical risk and fiscal costs
Tech and manufacturing job losses from lost China market access
Net negative employment in export-oriented sectors
Consumer electronics, goods prices rise; confidence dented
Limited direct exposure; offset by rate effects
CHIPS Act subsidies, defense spending, lower tax revenue

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Major power decoupling episodes rare (~5% per decade). But structural trend since 2018 (tariffs, CHIPS, export controls) creates path dependence. 2024 election cycle locks in bipartisan hawkishness. Adjusted to 22% for acceleration event (new sweeping controls) given legislative momentum. Pillar 6: diverse sources - USTR reports, semiconductor industry warnings, Chinese policy signals.

scenarios.name: Fiscal Crisis / Debt Ceiling Standoff
scenarios.description: Debt-to-GDP exceeds 125%. Treasury hits statutory limit in early 2027. Political brinkmanship triggers 6-week impasse, technical default risk, credit rating downgrade. Resolution involves spending caps but no revenue increases. Confidence shock raises borrowing costs permanently.

impacts.explanation: Higher interest costs compound; resolution lacks structural fix
Risk premium spikes on default fears; downgrade adds 30-50bps
Fed hikes to defend dollar and credibility amid fiscal dominance
Government spending cuts + uncertainty reduce investment
Federal contractor layoffs, state/local cuts, confidence channel
Dollar depreciation on fiscal fears raises import prices
Defense and infrastructure spending cuts hit manufacturing
Consumer confidence drops; federal worker furloughs
Mortgage rates jump on Treasury yield spike
Direct federal job cuts + private sector spillovers
Dollar weakness boosts exports; recession cuts imports

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Debt ceiling crises ~25% per Congress (2011, 2013, 2023). Current debt trajectory ($39.5T, +$1.5T/yr) makes 2027 binding. Tetlock adjustment: 15% (down from 25%) because divided government may force earlier resolution, and 2023 precedent created procedural workarounds. Commandment 8: 2011 error was underestimating market resilience; 2023 error was overestimating default risk.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overconfidence
Look for the errors behind your errors

scenarios.name: AI-Driven Productivity Surge
scenarios.description: Generative AI adoption reaches inflection point: enterprise deployment at scale, measurable TFP gains of 0.5-1% annually. White-collar automation accelerates. Investment boom in data centers, energy, semiconductors. Disinflationary as unit labor costs fall.

impacts.explanation: Productivity-driven growth above trend without overheating
AI reduces service-sector costs (coding, legal, admin, support)
Fed cuts faster as supply-side disinflation allows easier policy
Lower inflation expectations; higher real growth potential
Short-term displacement in automatable roles; transition friction
Job losses in some sectors offset by AI-complementary roles
Semiconductor, equipment, data center construction surge
Real income gains from lower prices; tech wealth effect
Lower rates + higher productivity wages support demand
Strong dollar on growth differential; import-intensive investment
Higher growth boosts revenue; lower rates reduce interest

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: General purpose technology inflections ~10% per decade (electricity, IT, internet). AI shows faster adoption curves but deployment lags. 10% reflects high potential but Solow paradox risk - productivity gains may take years to materialize in aggregate data. Pillar 3: continuous updating - Nvidia earnings, enterprise surveys, academic studies tracked monthly.

scenarios.name: Global Trade War Escalation
scenarios.description: Universal 10-20% tariffs enacted by US; retaliation by EU, China, others. WTO dispute system paralyzed. Global trade volumes contract 3-5%. Supply chains reconfigure under duress. Investment frozen by policy uncertainty. Stagflationary globally.

impacts.explanation: Tariffs reduce imports but retaliation hits exports harder; J-curve
Direct tariff pass-through + supply chain disruption costs
Trade contraction, uncertainty, inefficient production allocation
Manufacturing hit by input costs and export market loss
Fed fights tariff-driven inflation despite growth slowdown
Inflation premium + risk premium on fiscal/trade outlook
Export sector layoffs; investment strike reduces hiring
Net job losses in trade-exposed industries
Consumer prices up; confidence down; wealth effect negative
Higher rates + recession fears + material cost inflation
Tariff revenue offset by recessionary revenue loss + spending

scenarios.reasoning: Base rate: Global trade wars rare (~3% per decade: 1930s, 2018-19 limited). 2024 campaign rhetoric raises tail risk but institutional constraints (business lobby, Congress, allies) make universal tariffs unlikely. 5% reflects low probability but catastrophic impact. Pillar 2: outside view - Smoot-Hawley analogies often overused; modern economies more resilient. Commandment 4: don't overreact to political rhetoric.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence
Triage - Focus on questions where careful thinking pays off

methodology: Applied Tetlock's superforecasting framework: (1) Established base rates for each scenario class using historical frequencies (outside view). (2) Decomposed each scenario into causal mechanisms affecting each indicator (granular analysis). (3) Adjusted probabilities using inside-view evidence (current geopolitical tensions, policy momentum, economic data) while anchoring to base rates. (4) Assigned directional impacts with magnitude estimates for all 11 indicators per scenario. (5) Computed probability-weighted forecasts. (6) Assigned confidence intervals reflecting scenario dispersion and Knightian uncertainty. (7) Explicitly documented clashing causal forces and potential errors (Commandments 5, 8).
geopoliticalSummary: Elevated multi-theater tensions: Iran-Israel proxy conflict risks Strait of Hormuz disruption; Russia-Ukraine war persists with NATO-Russia escalation risks; China-Taiwan gray-zone pressure continues; Houthi Red Sea attacks disrupt Suez transit. US alliance architecture (AUKUS, Quad, NATO) holding but strained by burden-sharing debates. Global South non-alignment complicates sanctions enforcement. 2027 leadership transitions possible in several key states.
geoeconomicSummary: Fragmentation accelerating: friend-shoring and industrial policy (IRA, CHIPS, EU Green Deal) reshape supply chains. China's export dominance in green tech (solar, EVs, batteries) creates new dependencies. Dollar weaponization accelerates de-dollarization attempts (BRICS expansion, bilateral swap lines). Global trade growth below pre-2019 trend. Critical mineral competition intensifies. Services trade growing faster than goods.
currentEventsSummary: Fed in restrictive hold (3.88%) with inflation at 3.82% above target but trending down. Labor market cooling (UNRATE 4.1%, payrolls +0.1%) but resilient. GDP growth modest at 1.05%. Fiscal trajectory unsustainable: debt $39.5T (122% GDP), deficit >6% GDP. Housing recovery underway (starts +9.9%). Consumer spending soft (retail +0.2%). Industrial production contracting (-0.43%). 10-year yield at 4.92% reflects term premium. Key 2027 events: debt ceiling X-date, potential tariff legislation, AI infrastructure capex cycle.
